title: Cap. IV Arg. 6 Sol close: actual faith not foresight-faith; invert — nexus not Remonstrant order
pass_a_gloss: To these let it be added, That in all those places where the name of the Elect is attributed to the faithful, actual faith is always denoted, not that considered before the foundations of the world were laid in God's foresight alone, which the Remonstrants urge. They therefore do not rightly infer; Elect and believer are the same subjects according to the phrasing of the Scriptures: Therefore Election is made from foresight of faith; but, Therefore to all the elect in their time saving faith is given. I could easily invert this argument, and so twist it back against the adversaries, if it had any strength in itself, The word of Believers, when it is treated concerning believers unto salvation, is perpetually understood of the elect: Therefore there is no faith unto salvation except of the elect; Therefore faith arises from antecedent election. But from such use of vocabularies nothing else ought to be concluded than that faith and election have a certain nexus between them: but whether they are so connected that foresight of faith precedes election as a condition prerequired in electing, (which the Remonstrants will) or that faith follows election as a disposition to be produced in all the elect at the due time, does not stand from the places of Scripture brought. Therefore to weigh those one by one is least necessary.
pass_b_english: Add: wherever Elect is given to the faithful, actual faith is meant — not faith merely in God's foresight before the world's foundations, which the Remonstrants urge. So they wrongly infer: Elect and believer are the same subjects in Scripture's phrasing, therefore election is from foresight of faith. Rather: therefore to all the elect in their time saving faith is given. If the argument had force I could invert it: Believers, when salvation is in view, always means the elect; therefore no saving faith except of the elect; therefore faith arises from antecedent election. From such word-use you may conclude only that faith and election have a nexus — not whether foresight of faith precedes election as a prerequired condition (as Remonstrants will), or faith follows election as a disposition to be produced in all the elect at the due time. The cited places do not settle that; weighing them one by one is needless.
source_text: Hisce accedat, In illis omnibus locis ubi Electorum nomen tribuitur fidelibus, fidem actualem semper denotari, non illam ante jacta mundi fundamenta in sola Dei praescientia consideratam, quam urgent Remonstrantes. Non recte igitur inferunt; Electus et credens sunt subjecta eadem secundum phrasin Scripturarum: Ergo Electio fit ex praevisa fide; sed, Ergo omnibus electis suo tempore datur fides salutifera. Possem facile hoc argumentum invertere, et contra adversarios sic retorquere, si quid roboris in se haberet, Vox Credentium, cum de credentibus ad salutem agitur, perpetuo intelligitur de electis: Ergo nulla est fides ad salutem nisi electorum; Ergo fides oritur ex antecedente electione. Sed ex tali usu vocabulorum nihil aliud concludi debet, quam fidem et electionem habere inter se quendam nexum: sed utrum ita connectantur ut fides praevisa antecedat electionem tanquam conditio in eligendo praerequisita, (quod volunt Remonstrantes) an ut fides subsequatur electionem tanquam dispositio in omnibus electis debito tempore producenda, ex locis Scripturae allatis non constat. Ea igitur sigillatim expendere minime necessarium est.
